reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Auer rods prove myeloid lineage; faggot cells mean promyelocytic leukaemia
Start ATRA on suspicion of promyelocytic leukaemia before genetics return
Tumour lysis raises potassium, phosphate and urate while calcium falls
Childhood ALL is the commonest childhood malignancy
reference.pathophysiology: Acquired mutations block blast differentiation while driving proliferation, so immature clones crowd out normal haematopoiesis. Lineage, cytogenetics and molecular lesions determine behaviour and drug sensitivity, especially the retinoic acid receptor fusion that differentiation therapy exploits in promyelocytic disease.
additionalDifferentials: Promyelocytic leukaemia DIC versus other coagulopathies
additionalInvestigations: Marrow examination with flow cytometry and cytogenetics
Lumbar puncture for nervous system staging in ALL protocols
Uric acid, potassium, phosphate and calcium monitoring for tumour lysis
